description: The committed predicate-schema hash — the value a canonical world export stamps as `predicateSchemaHash` (schemas/canonical-world-export.schema.json) and a save file carries in its WorldSnapshot. Regenerated by US-1 when the KINP identity surface (id/3 + the identity rule pack) entered the schema, again by US-2 when the equivalence layer (same_as / based_on + the §4.3 firewall rules) did, again by US-3 when the world model (the @world(W) context argument + inheritance/override rules) did, and again by US-2 of 91-babylon-prolog-wasm when `sum_list/2` was renamed `insimul_sum_list/2` (the arity is unchanged, so the count did not move — only the name, and therefore the hash). That rename is required because the shared engine registers `sum_list/2` as a static builtin; see docs/tau-wasm-parity.md D-1. Regenerated once more by US-2 of 110-mechanic-predicate-vocabulary, which landed the mechanic vocabulary (docs/mechanic-predicates.md): 37 new fact predicates across the combat/perception/skill/traversal/equipment/stamina blocks plus four item-block extensions, and 9 runtime gameplay-state predicates (health/3, energy/3, has_equipped/3, …) that already existed in gameplay-predicates.ts but had never been registered anywhere the snapshot could see them. 612 → 658. And once more by US-3 of the same tasklist, which landed the seven mechanic RULE PACKS (src/prolog/mechanics/) in buildPredicateSchemaSnapshot()'s sources array: 27 clause heads the packs define — hostile_to/2, can_attack/2, detects/2, can_learn_skill/2, can_traverse/3, reachable/3, can_equip/2, encumbered/1, winded/1, stamina_regen/2 and the rest — which have to be inside the snapshot to be inside the builtin-collision guard. 658 → 685. And once more by US-1 of 113-game-ai-substrate, which landed the game-AI substrate's two packs (src/ai/perception-predicates.ts) in the same sources array: the perception-provenance pack's five runtime facts (agent_belief_world/2, percept/4, percept_channel/2, percept_actor/2, perceived/4) plus its rule heads (perceived/2, perceived_clearly/2, perceived_via/3, witness/2, unwitnessed/1, perceived_content/4) and the belief bridge's four (believes/4, unaware_of/3, mistaken/6, ignorant_of/5). Belief itself adds nothing: it is claim/4 at a belief world, read through the world pack's holds/4, so there is no belief predicate to register. 685 → 700. And once more by US-2 of the same tasklist, which landed the decision layer's pack (src/ai/action-predicates.ts): 17 names new to the snapshot — the legality gate and its enumeration (candidate_action/3, permissible/3, forbidden/3, forbidden_by/4, forbids/4, feasible/3, prerequisites_hold/3, action_target_choice/2), the scoring vocabulary (action_appeal/3, agent_motive/3, target_appeal/3, target_kind/2, action_bias/3) and the scalar projections a caller may bind to (action_cost/2, motive_appeal/5, action_requires_target/1, action_target_type/2). action/4, action_prerequisite/2 and can_perform/2,3 were already registered by the PREDICATE_SCHEMA action block, so the pack re-declaring them moves nothing. 700 → 717. And once more by US-3 of the same tasklist, which landed the rule-enforcement pack (src/ai/enforcement-predicates.ts): 16 names new to the snapshot — the authored norm vocabulary that turns an editor rule into a legality gate (rule_forbids_action/2, faction_law/2, faction_law_protects/2, norm_truth/3, norm_reputation/3), the two runtime facts (act/4, violation_record/4) and the rules that read them (norm/2, norm_kind/2, violation/5, violation_of/5, witnessed_violation/3, secret_violation/2, enforced_truth/5, enforced_reputation/5, agent_atom/2). forbids/4 does NOT move: the enforcement pack writes clauses for the predicate the decision pack already declared, which is the whole point — mores reach the gate by defining its input, not by widening it. rule_active/1, rule_category/2 and rule_applies/3 were already registered by the PREDICATE_SCHEMA rule block, and faction/2 and faction_stance/3 by the combat block. 717 -> 733. And once more by US-4 of the same tasklist, which landed the planning pack (src/ai/planning-predicates.ts): 14 names new to the snapshot — the authored goal vocabulary (goal/2, goal_requires/2, action_achieves/2, action_needs/2), the two runtime facts an NPC's errand lives in (agent_goal/3, condition_met/2) and the rules a planner reads (pursuing/3, goal_unmet/3, goal_satisfied/2, plan_step/4, projected_step/4, step_blocked/3, step_ready/2, goal_step/5). The action block does NOT move: a plan step is a (action, target) pair candidate_action/3 already yields, which is the whole of "one action vocabulary, not two". 733 -> 747. And once more by US-1 of 121-stealth-and-perception, which landed the graded detection state in the perception pack (src/prolog/mechanics/perception-predicates.ts): 7 names new to the snapshot — the three facts the ladder is made of (awareness/3 and detection_state/3 runtime, detection_threshold/2 authored and published at load the way stamina_threshold/2 is) and the four rules that name its rungs (suspicious_of/2, searching_for/2, noticed/2, undetected/1). alerted/2 does NOT move: the pack now derives it from detection_state/3 as well as declaring it dynamic, which adds a clause to a predicate the schema already registered — the boolean every authored rule already asks and the graded state cannot disagree. 747 -> 754. And once more by US-2 of 122-traversal-and-travel, which landed vehicles in the traversal block and pack (src/prolog/mechanics/traversal-predicates.ts): 9 names new to the snapshot — the four facts a ridden entity is made of (vehicle_mode/2 authored, published at load beside traversal_link/3; vehicle_owner/2, vehicle_occupant/2 and vehicle_driver/2 runtime, because a horse is bought, inherited and stolen) and the five rules that read them (riding_mode/2, can_board/2, can_drive/2, vehicle_unattended/1, vehicle_not_owned_by/2). at_location/2 does NOT move: a vehicle is an entity, and where an entity is already has a predicate every other rule reads. §12's cut of vehicle/1 and vehicle_capacity/2 still stands — vehicle_mode/2 says what a boat is by saying what it lends its driver, and speed and handling get no predicates at all (§11). 754 -> 763. Regenerated again by US-3 of 122-traversal-and-travel, which added fast travel to the same pack: can_fast_travel/2 (§7's own worked example, promoted from an authored can_perform/2 clause to a pack rule) plus the :- dynamic declaration of location_discovered/1, which is gameplay-predicates.ts's existing predicate rather than a travel-private copy of it — a place found through a rumour, a map or a quest is a place you may travel to. Elapsed world time gets no predicate at all: what a journey does to the world is that the CLOCK moved, and a fact asserting how long it took would be a second answer GameTimeManager already gives. 763 -> 765. Regenerated again by US-1 of 123-skill-trees-and-progression, which landed the skill TREE in the skill block and pack (src/prolog/mechanics/skill-predicates.ts): 12 names new to the snapshot — the seven facts a tree is made of (skill_tree/2, skill_node/2, skill_node_cost/2, skill_node_requires/2 and skill_node_effect/2 authored, published at load beside skill_level_xp/3; skill_points/3 and skill_unlocked/2 runtime, because what an actor has spent and taken is what two saves of one world differ by) and the five rules that read them (skill_goal_met/2, skill_node_price/2, skill_points_held/3, can_unlock/2, skill_effect/2). has_skill/3 does NOT move: progression RAISES a level, and the live level already has a predicate the whole rule library reads — a skill_level/3 beside it would be the second vocabulary for one fact §10.1 exists to prevent. No predicate is minted for what an action AWARDS or for how a node is DRAWN: the first is a property of the action the world already authors and the second is the host's entirely (§11). 765 -> 777. And once more by US-1 of 125-npc-routines-and-locomotion, which landed the routine pack (src/routines/routine-predicates.ts): 19 names new to the snapshot — the eight authored facts an NPC's day is made of (routine/2, routine_block/2, routine_block_window/3, routine_block_day/2, routine_block_goal/2, routine_block_place/2, routine_block_priority/2, routine_week_length/1), the two runtime facts (follows_routine/2, because an NPC takes a job and loses one, and routine_suspended/2, because what preempted a routine is a fact about one playthrough), the eight rules that read them (routine_weekday/1, routine_hour_in/3, routine_window_open/1, routine_day_matches/1, routine_due/2, routine_goal/3, routine_destination/2, routine_in_place/1) and — the one that is not the routine module's — day_number/1, which gameplay-predicates.ts has always declared and nothing had ever registered where the snapshot could see it. time_of_day/1 was already there; its companion was not, and a pack that reads the clock is the thing that noticed. agent_goal/3, goal_requires/2 and condition_met/2 do NOT move: the pack adds CLAUSES for predicates ai/planning-predicates.ts already declared, which is the whole point — a routine reaches the planner through the planner's own vocabulary rather than through one of its own, and a routine-owned goal predicate would be a goal the planner could not see. No predicate is minted for an action, a step or an animation: which action serves a routine goal is AgentPlanner's answer (§11, docs/npc-routines.md §2). 777 -> 796. And once more by US-1 of 133-map-and-geopolitical-layer, which landed the region and jurisdiction pack (src/geo/region-predicates.ts): 32 names new to the snapshot — the nine authored facts an extent is made of (region/1, region_kind/2, region_bounds/5, region_disc/4, region_biome/2, region_watershed/2, region_feature/2, place_position/3 and jurisdiction_law/2, the territorial twin of faction_law/2), the 22 rules that read them (in_region/3, region_size/2, smaller_region/2, region_at/4, region_terrain/2, position_terrain/3, position_biome/3, position_watershed/3, political_kind/1, geographic_kind/1, jurisdiction_level/2, jurisdiction_above/2, jurisdiction_of/3, innermost_jurisdiction/3, position_jurisdiction/4, jurisdiction_conflict/3, place_jurisdiction/3, place_of_settlement/2, agent_jurisdiction/3, in_jurisdiction/2, region_id/2, region_curie/2 — none of them recursive, which is why jurisdiction_of/3 exists at all), and scoped_norm/1 — the one name that is NOT the geo pack's. That last is the enforcement pack's new extension seam: a norm binds everyone unless something scoped it, faction_law/2 was the only scope until territory became one, and a predicate is how a third scope gets added later without editing the universal clause again. forbids/4 does NOT move: the geo pack writes clauses for the predicate the decision pack already declared, so a border reaches the legality gate through the same seam a social more does. Neither do country/1, state/1, settlement/1, settlement_of_state/2, state_of_country/2 or the terrain predicates — they are the PREDICATE_SCHEMA country/state/settlement blocks', declared dynamic in the pack so it loads alone rather than to claim them, which is the whole of "a region is the document's extent and not a parallel structure". The short names are why registration matters here: region/1, in_region/3 and region_at/4 are exactly the shape a Prolog engine may own, and a containment test that silently resolved to a builtin would put every actor in the wrong country. 796 -> 828. And once more by US-2 of the same tasklist, which landed political history (src/geo/history-predicates.ts): 32 names new to the snapshot. 28 are the temporal pack's — the one authored fact a regime is dated by (era_interval/3), the regime lookups (era_world/1, era_at/2, era_before_end/2, era_starts_before/2, era_at_curie/2 and era_overlap/2, which names a history that governs one instant twice rather than resolving it), the world-relative extent (region_extent_at_world/3, region_extent_stated/2, region_extent_shape/1, region_extent_during/4 — the interval a border was valid over), the world-relative geometry and chain (in_region_at_world/4, region_size_at_world/3, smaller_region_at_world/3, region_at_world/5, jurisdiction_parent_at_world/3, jurisdiction_parent_stated/2, jurisdiction_above_at_world/3, jurisdiction_of_at_world/4, innermost_jurisdiction_at_world/4, position_jurisdiction_at_world/5, jurisdiction_conflict_at_world/4, place_jurisdiction_at_world/4) and the five time-indexed entry points a caller actually asks (region_at_time/5, position_jurisdiction_at_time/5, jurisdiction_conflict_at_time/4, place_jurisdiction_at_time/4, agent_jurisdiction_at_time/4). The other 4 are US-1's own arithmetic lifted out of in_region/3 and region_size/2 so both layers share one containment test instead of drifting apart: region_extent/2, region_extent_contains/3, region_extent_area/2, and jurisdiction_parent/2, the single chain step jurisdiction_above/2 is now two clauses over. claim/4 and world_resolve/4 do NOT move, and that is the whole claim of the story: a regime is a KINP world, a border is a claim at it, and resolving one as of a time is the inheritance layer identity/world-predicates.ts already provides — a second temporal mechanism would have shown up here as a second set of names. The short ones are again why registration matters: era_at/2 and era_world/1 are exactly the shape an engine may own, and a regime lookup that resolved to a builtin would date every border to whenever the builtin felt like. 828 -> 860. And once more by US-3 of 136-whole-game-scaffolding, which landed the scaffold rule pack (src/scaffold/scaffold-predicates.ts): 32 names new to the snapshot — the sixteen authored facts a game's shell is made of (scaffold/1, scaffold_genre/2, scaffold_world/2, scaffold_seed/2, scaffold_module/2, the four scaffold_start_* , scaffold_objective/5, the three scaffold_stage_*, the two scaffold_ending_* and scaffold_edited/2), the ONE runtime fact the layer remembers (scaffold_active/1 — which scaffold this playthrough is running, and nothing else, because a stage is open because the world is a certain way and a second copy of that could disagree), and the fifteen rules that read them (scaffold_holds/1, scaffold_in_play/1, scaffold_start/4, scaffold_start_unjustified/2, scaffold_stage_open/2, scaffold_stage_blocked/2, scaffold_current_stage/2, scaffold_objective_gated/2, scaffold_objective_unlocked/2, scaffold_objective_available/2, scaffold_objective_locked/2, scaffold_progress/3, scaffold_ending_reached/3, scaffold_over/1, scaffold_outcome/2). Every name is scaffold-prefixed and therefore safe from a builtin collision by construction, but registration matters here for the other half of the reason: scaffold_holds/1 is the one meta-call in the build that runs AUTHORED goals through call/1, and a clause head of this pack refused by a strict engine would take the whole pack down and leave every gate permanently closed with nothing raised. No mechanic predicate moves and none is added: a gate is a goal in whatever vocabulary the genre activated, which is the whole of "the scaffold selects from the mechanics that exist and invents none". 860 -> 892. Regenerated again by US-2 of 124-items-equipment-economy, which added trade to the equipment area: three authored predicates that join an item to the simulation (vendor/2, vendor_markup/2, item_stock_normal/2), item_loot_weight/2 for the rarity the IR always carried and no predicate said, gold/2 registered at last, and the pack rules over them (stock_level/3, in_stock/3, sells/2, scarce/2, proceeds_to/2, can_pay/2). No price predicate: §12. 892 -> 903. Regenerated again by US-3 of 124-items-equipment-economy, which added PLACEMENT to the same area: one minted fact predicate, item_at/3 — the fourth place an item can be, and the only one the vocabulary had no fact for — plus the two pack rules over it (item_here/2, container_here/2). Nothing else moves, and that is the finding: containers already had five predicates in helper-predicates.ts, a chest that is somewhere is at_location/2 like a boat (§7), and a loot table gets no predicate at all because it is authored content core computes over (§11), exactly as a price is. 903 -> 906.
algorithm: sha256 over the newline-joined, canonically sorted `name/arity` list of buildPredicateSchemaSnapshot() — see hashPredicateSchema() in src/prolog/predicate-schema.ts. `kind` is deliberately excluded.
regenerate: write a one-line script importing src/prolog/predicate-schema and printing hashPredicateSchema(buildPredicateSchemaSnapshot()) + the snapshot length, then run it with `npx vite-node <script>` (this vite-node build has no `-e` flag, and tsx is not a dependency). Simpler still: read the value the drift test prints on failure, then commit it together with the schema change.
